ZZ Rules of Civil Evidence (SYNTHETIC)
Synthetic test data. This is not real law of any jurisdiction.

Rule 1. Scope. These rules govern the admission of evidence in civil proceedings in the courts of ZZ.
Rule 2. Relevance. Evidence is relevant if it has any tendency to make a fact of consequence to the action more or less probable than it would be without the evidence. Irrelevant evidence is not admissible.
Rule 3. Burden of proof. The party asserting a fact bears the burden of proving it. The standard of proof in civil proceedings is the balance of probabilities.
Rule 4. Hearsay. A statement made out of court and offered to prove the truth of what it asserts is hearsay and is not admissible except as provided by these rules.
Rule 5. Business records. A record made in the regular course of business at or near the time of the event it records is not excluded by Rule 4.
Rule 6. Original documents. To prove the content of a writing, the original is required, unless the original is lost or a duplicate is admitted by agreement.
Rule 7. Electronic records. An email or other electronic record may be authenticated by evidence that it was sent from or received at an address associated with the person concerned.
Rule 8. Witnesses. A witness may testify only to matters within the witness's personal knowledge.
Rule 9. Expert opinion. A witness qualified as an expert may give an opinion if specialised knowledge will help the court understand the evidence.
Rule 10. Admissions. A statement by a party offered against that party is not hearsay.
